fullPassage: A conceptual model is an explanation, usually highly simplified, of how something works. It doesn't have to be complete or even accurate as long as it is useful. The files, folders, and icons you see displayed on a computer screen help people create the conceptual model of documents and folders inside the computer, or of apps or applications on the screen. In fact, there are no folders inside the computer — those are effective conceptualizations designed to make them easier to use. Sometimes these depictions can add to the confusion, however. When reading e-mail or visiting a website, the material appears to be on the device, for that is where it is displayed and used. But in fact, in many cases the actual material is "in the cloud," located on some distant machine. The conceptual model is of one, coherent image, whereas it may actually consist of parts, each located on different machines that could be almost anywhere in the world.

The conceptual model is of one, coherent image, whereas it may actually consist of parts, each located on different machines that could be almost anywhere in the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.ref: 원문: 'the actual material is in the cloud, located on some distant machine'
det.correct: ③ 많은 경우 실제 자료는 먼 기계에 위치한 클라우드에 있다: 원문 일치.
wrongs: ① 개념적 모델은 항상 정확하다: 'doesn't have to be accurate' → 반대
② 컴퓨터에는 실제 폴더가 있다: 'no folders' → 반대
④ 이메일은 항상 기기에 저장된다: 'in the cloud' → 반대
det.tip: 원문: 'in many cases the actual material is in the cloud, located on some distant machine'.

ch: 많은 경우 실제 자료는 먼 기계에 위치한 클라우드에 있다.
이메일 자료는 항상 사용자 기기에 저장된다.

questions.passage: A conceptual model is an explanation, usually highly simplified, of how something works. It doesn't have to be complete or even accurate as long as it is useful. The files, folders, and icons you see displayed on a computer screen help people create the conceptual model of documents and folders inside the computer, or of apps or applications on the screen. In fact, there are no folders inside the computer — those are effective conceptualizations designed to make them easier to use. Sometimes these depictions can add to the confusion, however. When reading e-mail or visiting a website, the material appears to be on the device, for that is where it is displayed and used. But in fact, in many cases the actual material is "in the cloud," located on some distant machine. The conceptual model is of one, coherent image, whereas it may actually consist of parts, each located on different machines that could be almost anywhere in the world.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 필자가 "those are effective conceptualizations"라고 한 함축적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.ref: effective conceptualizations = 실제가 아니지만 유용한 가상의 표현.
det.correct: ① 실제가 아니더라도 사용자에게 유용하면 가치가 있다: effective(효과적) + conceptualizations(개념화, 가상) → 유용성 강조.
wrongs: ② 모든 컴퓨터 아이콘은 제거해야 한다: 반대(effective라고 긍정적 평가)
③ 사용자는 컴퓨터 구조를 완벽히 이해해야 한다: doesn't have to be accurate → 반대
④ 가상 표현은 항상 혼란을 준다: sometimes → 항상은 아님
det.tip: effective(효과적) = 긍정적 평가. 실제가 아니지만(no folders) 유용하다(easier to use).

ch: 실제가 아니더라도 사용자에게 유용하면 가치가 있다.
컴퓨터의 모든 아이콘은 즉시 제거해야 한다.
사용자는 컴퓨터의 실제 구조를 완벽히 이해해야 한다.
가상의 표현은 항상 사용자에게 혼란을 준다.

questions.passage: When reading e-mail or visiting a website, the material appears to be on the device, for that is where it is __________ (display) and used. But in fact, in many cases the actual material is "in the cloud."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.ref: display → displayed: 수동태(be + p.p.). it is displayed = 그것이 표시된다.
det.correct: displayed: is __ and used → be동사 + 과거분사(수동태). display의 과거분사 = displayed.
det.tip: be + p.p. = 수동태. is displayed and used = 표시되고 사용된다.

questions.passage: A conceptual model is an explanation, usually highly __________ (simple), of how something works. It doesn't have to be complete or even accurate as long as it is useful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.ref: simple(형용사) → simplified(과거분사/형용사): highly __(부사+형용사 구조). '단순화된'이라는 의미.
det.correct: simplified: simple → simplify(동사화) → simplified(과거분사). highly simplified = 매우 단순화된.
det.tip: simple → simplify(동사) → simplified(p.p./형용사). highly + 형용사 = 매우 ~한.
